title: Learning while it sleeps
blurb: After a day of practice, the model studies what it found and settles it in. Here is how the sleep modes work, what they scored, and what is only planned.

scenes.heading: Sleep sorts out the day

caption.text: People sort out the day's lessons while they sleep.
This model gets a night too: a day of practice, then a night of study.
Sleep is not a sixth part. It is a way of learning, tested so far only in research on earlier-design copies.

scenes.heading: By day: a puzzle with a hidden rule

caption.text: By day the model gets puzzles with a hidden rule: 2 gives 5, 4 gives 9, 7 gives 15.
It tries rules. A try counts only if it fits every example, so no answer key is needed.
Only x times 2 plus 1 fits all three, so 10 gives 21. That try is kept, and the night studies it.

scenes.heading: The old sleep and the newer sleep

caption.text: The old sleep scored 71.3 out of 100 on first tries and needed 558 to 610 updates by its formula. An update is a small nudge to every setting.
The newer sleep used 256 updates a night and averaged 76.1 over six copies.
But this is not a paired comparison. 71.3 is the old sleep's stored number, from its own near-copy starting copies. Each copy slept once.

scenes.heading: One night of the newer sleep

caption.text: The model makes its own tries, then sleeps for 256 updates of 1,024 rows. A row is one practice question.
Half the rows are fresh dreams: new questions written from a program it found, so none is read twice. Half are fresh skills rows.
Every 32 updates it checks itself on 128 held questions, and keeps its best saved model.

scenes.notes: Flags drawn are one per 32 updates (256 / 32 = 8, not written on screen). Picture only.

scenes.heading: Did sleep earn the credit?

caption.text: Did old skills get worse than before the sleep? No. Pooled over the six copies they rose by 0.52 points, likely range 0.31 to 0.74.
But a control that only practised the same skills rows raised them by 2.11, range 1.88 to 2.32.
So sleep did not beat plain practice: sleep minus control is −1.58. The gain is not shown to come from the sleep.

scenes.heading: New since Oct 9: two nights in a row

caption.text: A two-night recipe, SCM2, passed its test on 2 copies: night, a day of search, night. Reported, not rechecked.
Skills score, out of 100. Copy 1: 86.7 before, 82.9 after the standard two nights, 87.8 after SCM2.
Copy 2: 87.8 before, 84.7 after the standard two nights, 89.3 after SCM2. No forgetting.
Learning kept up. On multi-step puzzles, first try against the standard two nights was −1.9 and +1.9. The pass mark was no worse than −2.
Only 2 copies so far. A check on more copies is still to come.

scenes.heading: Planned: sleep inside the first big run

caption.text: Planned, not done: sleep becomes part of the first big training run.
The 100M training itself stays as it is. After it comes a day-and-night phase, and the SCM2 nights are its recipe.
First it must pass on smaller test models, at 3M and then 10M. Those tests have not run yet. Results so far are from earlier-design copies.
Planned time: about a week after the main training. An estimate, not measured.

scenes.heading: What to remember

caption.text: Sleep is a night of study after a day of practice. The newer sleep scored 76.1 in 256 updates, not in a paired test.
Two nights in a row kept old skills on 2 copies. Sleep in the first big run is planned, not done.
